title: Results
description: v1 contract (task M5-T125, directive D-090 Wave 0; derived lane plan docs/lanes/PARALLEL_BUILD_PLAN.md section 5) for the results of ONE option at ONE study revision (plan docs/PRODUCT_PLAN_CURRENT_2026-09-28.md sections 5, 5a, 5b, 5c, 9, 11b; tasks M1-14, M1-25). Holds the three SEPARATE answers - floor-area allowance, permitted envelope, building option - each either available (values with units, Zoning Resolution sections and sources) or 'not_available' with a reason, never a number with a caution label (section 5 'Calculation behavior', section 5a item 3); remaining floor area after a kept building (section 3 step 4); the shortfall between the building option and the allowance, whose reasons are computed from named constraints (section 5 answer 3; competitor-review checks C-2, C-11); optional add-on gains relative to the current selection and 'Best combination' with its goal and exclusions (section 5; M1-25); the completeness line; the status strip (at most three items, section 5a item 1); the floor-by-floor table and floor stack (section 5); the keep / partial-rebuild / full-rebuild paths (section 5b); the unit estimate with its formula, in one place (section 11b; check C-12); ONE geometry block in feet that the screen drawings, PDF and DXF all read (section 5c item 1; checks C-4, C-5); and the rule versions used (section 9). Every drawing label and report figure is read from this document, never typed (section 5c item 5).

contract_version.description: CLOSED enum of published results contract versions. 1.0.0 = M5-T125 initial shape (D-090 Wave 0). 1.1.0 (D-090-R108) adds the OPTIONAL top-level 'scope' object (purpose: put the scope beside the numbers - the headline cards and exported drawings visibly carry the 'Tax-lot-only estimate' label, identify the lot, and disclose the assumed corner conditions, while whole-site and remaining capacity stay unconfirmed). scope is OPTIONAL and may be absent or null; a document carrying a NON-NULL scope object declares 1.1.0 (the version-binding allOf below), while a document with an absent or null scope may declare 1.0.0 or 1.1.0, so every valid 1.0.0 instance stays valid unchanged. 1.2.0 (D-090-R132) adds the OPTIONAL 'notes' array on the building-option answer only (purpose: carry the engine's COMPUTED minimum-base-height note into the results document so it can be shown beside the heights instead of being dropped before the document; DB-119). notes is OPTIONAL and may be absent, null or empty; a document whose building-option answer carries a NON-EMPTY notes array declares 1.2.0 (the version-binding allOf below), while a document with an absent, null or empty notes array may declare 1.0.0, 1.1.0 or 1.2.0, so every valid 1.0.0 and 1.1.0 instance stays valid byte-for-byte. 1.3.0 (M5-T128, work order docs/plans/R6B_RESULTS_CONNECTION_WORK_ORDER_2026-10-06.md section 0 'How a result may appear', decision D5; D-090-R229/R255/R258/R268) lets ONE value inside an answer carry which of the three ways it appears in. It adds (a) the OPTIONAL 'value_states' object on each AVAILABLE answer (floor_area_allowance, permitted_envelope and the building option): a map keyed by the answer value's key, each entry declaring the value's way - 'settled' (no condition), 'conditional' (one or more named conditions, each with its kind, the assumption in words and what would settle it) or 'withheld' (no number; its label, reason, which of the two gap kinds it is, what would resolve it, and the law section where one applies); and (b) the OPTIONAL 'resolved_by' and 'gap_kind' fields on a whole-answer 'not available' object, so a withheld whole answer can also say what would resolve it and which gap kind it is. value_states and the not-available resolution fields are OPTIONAL and additive: a document carrying ANY of them declares 1.3.0 (the version-binding allOf below), and a document declaring 1.3.0 carries a non-empty way-layer on every available answer (the forward-binding allOf below), each entry present stating one way; stating the way of every shown value, so none is settled by silence, is the emitter's rule, refused by the validator of the engine that emits this version, not by this schema; a document carrying none of them may declare 1.0.0, 1.1.0 or 1.2.0, so every valid 1.0.0 / 1.1.0 / 1.2.0 instance stays valid byte-for-byte. The remaining-floor-area line is UNCHANGED (it keeps the shared not_available shape). The enum is append-only (new versions are admitted only by an accepted contract task that appends to it); the emitter decides when to declare a higher version.

revision.description: The study revision these results were computed for (study.revision.number).

out_of_date.description: True when a site input, this option, or a rule version changed after computation (plan section 9 'Dependency-based invalidation'); rows then carry the 'Out of date' exception (section 5a item 3). A source a fact uses being behind a newer published version (check C-7, data side; services/api/app/profile/data_versions.py) is also an 'Out of date' condition: it is surfaced per row through the exception_label 'Out of date' from DataVersionReport.fact_exception_labels(). Whether a behind source also sets this top-level out_of_date flag is left to the wiring step (request docs/lanes/requests/B-1.md) and is not fixed by this contract; the per-source status itself travels on site_fact source.version_check (site_fact contract 1.1.0).

out_of_date_reason.description: Why the results are out of date; null when current.

depends_on_fact_ids.description: The site_fact.fact_id values these results were computed from (plan section 9 invalidation).

lot_selection_statement.const: Based on the lots you selected — the app does not verify the zoning lot
lot_selection_statement.description: The exact label results carry (plan section 3 step 2; check C-9).

with_approvals_label.description: 'With approvals — not guaranteed' while any agreement or approval add-on (catalog groups C, D1) is on; null otherwise (plan section 5).

answers.description: The three separate answers (plan section 5). Each is shown only when its rules are implemented and reviewed, eligibility is resolved and the site geometry is supported; otherwise it is 'not_available' with the reason. Every supported answer still shows.

floor_area_allowance.description: The most zoning floor area the rules allow on the site (FAR x lot area, with applicable add-ons). The existing-building subtraction is reported separately in remaining_floor_area.

permitted_envelope.description: The three-dimensional limits: base and maximum heights, setbacks, yards and lot coverage.

building_option.description: A generated building inside the envelope and within the allowance: achieved floor area, floors, height, footprint width x depth. This is the only answer that may carry the OPTIONAL additive 'notes' array (contract 1.2.0, D-090-R132): COMPUTED, plain-English draft readings such as the minimum-base-height note. The other two answers use the plain answer shape with no notes slot.

remaining_floor_area.description: Allowance minus the existing ZONING floor area when a building stays (plan section 3 step 4, section 5 answer 1). Without an established or entered existing zoning floor area it is not_available with the reason 'Needs verified zoning-lot boundaries and existing zoning floor area.' and shows as 'Remaining development capacity: Not confirmed' (owner wording, D-090-R038), while the full-site allowance still shows. not_applicable when no building is kept.

shortfall.description: Gap between the building option and the allowance (plan section 5 answer 3; checks C-2 and C-11). 'none' when the option reaches the allowance.

addon_gains.description: Each optional add-on with what it would add to (or, when on, contributes to) the CURRENT selection and what it requires (plan section 5). Gains are computed by recalculating everything together, never added up. Group D2 (variances, rezonings) never produces a number and is never listed here.

best_combination.description: 'Best combination' for a stated goal: only supported, quantified group A and B add-ons; shows why anything was left out (plan section 5; M1-25).

completeness_line.description: E.g. 'Add-ons checked for this district: all 12', or 'Not yet covered: X, Y' (plan section 5 'Also shown').

status_strip.description: One status strip at the top of the results: at most three short items, e.g. 'Zoning maximum · approximate measurements · lots you selected' (plan section 5a item 1). Tapping it opens the details and the standing notices.

notices_count.description: Number of standing notices behind the strip, shown as one 'Notes (N)' item (plan section 5a items 2 and 6). The notice texts live in report_model.standing_notices.

floor_by_floor.description: Floor-by-floor area table computed from the same data as the building option: gross area, deductions and zoning floor area per floor (plan section 5; section 3 step 7). Empty when the building option is not available.

floor_stack.description: How many floors fit under the height limits, with the floor-to-floor heights used and the allowable area of each floor where setbacks shrink upper floors (plan section 5 'Floor stack').

existing_building.description: Keep, partly rebuild, or rebuild (plan section 5b; task M2-08; check C-3).

unit_estimate.description: Dwelling-unit estimate with its formula, in ONE place; every screen, sheet and file repeats this value (plan section 11b; check C-12).

geometry.description: The ONE geometry source the site plan, section, 3D massing, PDF and DXF all read (plan section 5c items 1-3). not_available only when not even the lot outline is known; otherwise geometry_available with each rule-dependent layer available or not_available.

rule_versions.description: Every rule table version these results used (plan section 9: a new rule version marks every result that uses it).

draft.description: Machine-readable draft marker (G3 M-4). true when ANY rule_versions entry is not 'published' (qualified-reviewer approval). While draft is true, a surface shown to an architect renders every available answer as 'not_available' with reason_kind 'rule_not_reviewed' (plan section 5 'Calculation behavior'; D-090-R010), unless the surface sits behind a lane flag. false is admitted only when every rule_versions entry is 'published'.

street_width_case.description: Plan section 4 'Needs street width' (G3 RC-2). null = these results do not depend on an unknown street width. Otherwise this document is ONE case of a side-by-side set: it was computed with the stated wide/narrow assumption for each street whose width fact is unknown, and it names the sibling results document(s) of the other case(s) for the same study, option and revision. Surfaces show the cases side by side, marked 'Needs street width'; values that differ between the cases carry exception_label 'Needs street width'. In a case, the assumed width counts as an 'assumed' input for an answer's weakest-input label. The street_width site fact itself stays unknown (site_fact.schema.json).

scope.description: OPTIONAL scope-beside-the-numbers block (contract 1.1.0, D-090-R108). Puts the scope next to the figures so the headline cards and the exported drawings visibly state 'Tax-lot-only estimate' (label), identify the lot (lot.display), disclose the assumed corner conditions (assumptions[].statement), and keep whole-site and remaining capacity unconfirmed (whole_site, remaining_capacity). The face reads label, lot.display, the assumptions' statements, and the two settled strings (remaining_capacity.label and remaining_capacity.reason) directly from this block, never typed. Every value is derived deterministically by the emitter from the study inputs (the lot fields from the BBL). OPTIONAL in this contract (a later PR may require it once the engine emits it); absent or null is valid. A non-null object binds contract_version to 1.1.0 (the version-binding allOf below).

_expected_failure.description: FIXTURE-ONLY annotation stating the intended defect of an invalid fixture (packages/contracts README convention). Producers NEVER emit this key.

allOf.description: out_of_date true needs a reason; false has none.
draft false only when every rule version is published (D-090-R010: nothing is presented as reviewed without review).

Version binding (contract 1.1.0, D-090-R108; widened to the enum by D-090-R132/R137, DB-129): a document carrying a non-null scope object declares contract_version 1.1.0 OR 1.2.0, not const 1.1.0. 1.2.0 is a strict superset of 1.1.0 - the scope object is allowed AND the building-option notes array is allowed - so a single document may carry BOTH a non-null scope and a non-empty notes array and still declare a valid version (it resolves to 1.2.0). Before this widening the scope clause pinned const 1.1.0 while the notes clause (the allOf below) pins const 1.2.0, so a document carrying both was unsatisfiable: no single contract_version could satisfy both clauses (the scope emitter and the notes emitter each fire on the R6B 215-16 Northern path). An absent or null scope still leaves the version unconstrained, so every 1.0.0 instance stays valid. Expressed as anyOf (not if/then) so the stdlib and engine validators agree: either scope is null (or absent, since 'properties' is vacuous for an absent key), or contract_version is one of 1.1.0 / 1.2.0. The notes binding below is unchanged (a non-empty notes array still binds to const 1.2.0), so a document with both a scope and non-empty notes resolves to exactly 1.2.0, while a scope-only document stays valid at either 1.1.0 or 1.2.0.

Version binding (contract 1.2.0, D-090-R132): a document whose building-option answer carries a NON-EMPTY notes array declares contract_version 1.2.0. An absent, null or empty notes array leaves the version unconstrained, so 1.0.0 and 1.1.0 stay valid for it. Expressed as anyOf (not if/then) so the stdlib and engine validators agree: either the building-option notes array is null or empty (or absent, since 'properties' is vacuous for an absent key, and a not_available building option has no notes key), or contract_version is 1.2.0.

Version binding (contract 1.3.0, M5-T128, work order section 0 / decision D5; D-090-R229/R255/R258/R268): REVERSE direction. A document carrying ANY 1.3.0 field declares contract_version 1.3.0. The 1.3.0 fields are the OPTIONAL 'value_states' map on any available answer (floor_area_allowance, permitted_envelope or the building option) and the OPTIONAL 'resolved_by' / 'gap_kind' fields on a whole-answer not-available object. Expressed as anyOf (not if/then) so the stdlib and engine validators agree: either NONE of the three answers carries a value_states map or a not-available resolution field (each is null or absent - 'properties' is vacuous for an absent key, and an available answer has no resolved_by/gap_kind key, a not-available answer has no value_states key), or contract_version is 1.3.0. An absent/null value_states and absent resolution fields leave the version unconstrained, so every 1.0.0 / 1.1.0 / 1.2.0 instance stays valid byte-for-byte.

Version binding (contract 1.3.0, M5-T128, work order section 0 property (c); D-090-R268): FORWARD direction. This clause enforces that a document declaring 1.3.0 carries a non-empty value_states map on every AVAILABLE answer (status 'available'), and - through value_state - that every entry present declares a way ('settled', 'conditional' or 'withheld'). A not-available answer has no values and needs no value_states map. This clause does NOT enforce that there is an entry for every value shown in an answer's 'values' array: JSON Schema 2020-12 cannot compare the keys of the two. Giving one entry for every shown value, so none is settled by silence, is the contract's rule all the same - the emitter's duty, refused by the validator of the engine that emits this version, not by this schema. Expressed as anyOf (not if/then) so the stdlib and engine validators agree: either contract_version is 1.0.0 / 1.1.0 / 1.2.0 (this clause then imposes nothing, so every earlier instance stays valid byte-for-byte), or every answer is either not-available (status const 'not_available') or carries a value_states map (required).

value_states.description: OPTIONAL per-value way-layer for an AVAILABLE answer (contract 1.3.0, M5-T128, work order section 0 / decision D5). A map keyed by the answer value's key (the same key namespace as answer_value.key): each entry declares which of the three ways that value appears in - settled, conditional or withheld (value_state below). A shown value (settled or conditional) keeps its present value object and number in the answer's 'values' array (nothing is duplicated here, and value_state carries no number); a withheld value must have no entry in 'values' (it carries no number anywhere) and appears only here with its label, reason, gap kind, what would resolve it and, where one applies, the law section. One entry states exactly one way: an entry that mixes the fields of two ways matches no branch and is refused. This schema does NOT compare the keys of the 'values' list with the keys of this map, so it does not refuse (i) a shown value that has no entry here, nor (ii) a key that is shown in 'values' and marked withheld here. Both are rules of the contract all the same: the emitter must give one entry for every shown value and must never mark a shown key withheld, and the validator of the engine that emits this version must refuse a document that breaks either. OPTIONAL and additive: absent or null leaves the contract version unconstrained; a non-null map binds contract_version to 1.3.0 (the reverse version-binding allOf above), and a document declaring 1.3.0 must carry a non-empty map on every available answer (the forward version-binding allOf above).

value_state.description: One value's way (contract 1.3.0, work order section 0 'How a result may appear'): exactly one of settled, conditional or withheld, discriminated by 'way'. Each branch is closed (additionalProperties false), so an entry that mixes fields of two ways - e.g. a settled entry carrying a condition or a reason, or a withheld entry carrying a number or a condition - matches no branch and is rejected; an entry that states no 'way' is rejected.

oneOf.description: SETTLED: every fact behind the value comes from evidence, a reference case supports the reading of the law, and every condition that could change it has been checked (work order section 0). The number, its law section and its sources live in the matching entry of the answer's 'values' array (the emitter's rule; this schema does not cross-check the two). A settled value carries NO condition (no 'conditions' key).

CONDITIONAL: the value rests on one or more explicit, defensible assumptions that are not evidence (work order section 0). The number lives in the matching entry of the answer's 'values' array (the emitter's rule; this schema does not cross-check the two); this entry names at least one condition, each with its kind, the assumption in words and what would settle it. 'If <the assumption>: <the number>'.

way.description: This value is conditional on the assumptions listed in 'conditions'.

conditions.description: The assumptions the value rests on (at least one). A conditional value with an empty or absent list is rejected.

oneOf.description: WITHHELD: a known gap affects the value and no defensible condition covers it (work order section 0). It carries NO number (no 'value' or number key). It is listed here beside the shown values of the same answer, with its label, the reason, which of the two gap kinds it is, what would resolve it and, where one applies, the law section.

label.description: The human label of the withheld value, e.g. 'Maximum lot coverage' (the key itself is the value_states map key).

reason.description: Why it is not known, e.g. 'The lot reaches 103.93 ft from the 215 Place street line, beyond the 100 ft corner-coverage area; the ZR 12-10 corner definition is not captured.'

resolved_by.description: What would resolve the gap, e.g. 'Capturing the ZR 12-10 corner definition and reading it against the recorded outline.'

zr_sections.description: The Zoning Resolution section(s) the withheld value would rely on, where one applies (OPTIONAL).

value_condition.description: One explicit, defensible assumption behind a CONDITIONAL value (work order section 0 'conditional'; owner rules 1 and 3, R255/R257). Names the assumption, its kind and what would settle it. A conditional value carries at least one; a settled value carries none.

kind.description: The kind of assumption (work order section 0): 'user_statement' = a user's statement about the lot, used only for a clearly labelled conditional result and never stored as a fact (R255; e.g. the special-density-area answer, gap K11); 'contradicted_record' = a recorded figure that another recorded figure contradicts (R257; e.g. the two lot-area figures, gap K5); 'unchecked_condition' = a condition that was not checked and is assumed not to apply (R268; e.g. the K20 conditions - waterfront, airport height, transit easement, a lot near a district line).

assumption.description: The assumption in plain words, as the face shows it, e.g. 'If the recorded lot area of 10,075 sq ft is confirmed' or 'If none of the unchecked conditions (waterfront, airport height, transit easement, near a district line) applies to this lot'.

settled_by.description: What would settle the assumption (make the value settled, or withhold it), e.g. 'A survey or deed dimensions' or 'Capturing and reading the governing law text, then confirming the condition is absent'.

gap_kind.description: Which of the two kinds a withheld value or a withheld whole answer is (owner rule 4, R258): 'missing_information' = something only this property's evidence can settle is not known; 'work_owed' = a promised feature the program has not built yet. The two are never conflated: calling unfinished work 'unsupported' does not finish it.

answer_not_available.description: The 'not available' shape for a WHOLE answer (floor_area_allowance, permitted_envelope or the building option). It is the shared not_available shape (status, reason, reason_kind) PLUS the OPTIONAL additive 1.3.0 fields 'resolved_by' and 'gap_kind' (M5-T128, work order property (f)), so a withheld whole answer can also say what would resolve it and which of the two gap kinds it is, WITHOUT changing the present required fields. Every valid 1.0.0 / 1.1.0 / 1.2.0 not-available answer (no resolved_by / gap_kind key) stays valid byte-for-byte because both are optional and absent is allowed; a NON-NULL resolved_by or gap_kind binds contract_version to 1.3.0 (the reverse version-binding allOf above). The shared not_available def is UNCHANGED and still used everywhere else (remaining_floor_area, shortfall, the geometry layers, add-on gains, etc.), so nothing outside the three answers changes.

reason_kind.description: Which section 5 condition failed: a missing number, a missing or unreviewed rule, unresolved eligibility, or unsupported geometry (plan sections 5 and 8). Same vocabulary as the shared not_available.

resolved_by.description: OPTIONAL (contract 1.3.0): what would resolve this whole withheld answer, in plain words, e.g. 'Capturing and reading the Article III sections that govern a residential building in a commercial overlay, then a reference case'. Absent or null for a 1.0.0 / 1.1.0 / 1.2.0 answer.

gap_kind.description: OPTIONAL (contract 1.3.0): which of the two gap kinds this whole withheld answer is - missing information or work the program still owes (owner rule 4, R258). Absent or null for a 1.0.0 / 1.1.0 / 1.2.0 answer.

scope.description: The scope-beside-the-numbers block (contract 1.1.0, D-090-R108). Puts the scope next to the figures: basis and label name the estimate ('Tax-lot-only estimate'), lot identifies it, whole_site keeps whole-site development unconfirmed, remaining_capacity keeps remaining development capacity not confirmed with the two owner-settled strings, and assumptions discloses the assumed corner conditions in plain English. The face shows label, lot.display, the assumptions' statements, and the two settled strings (remaining_capacity.label and remaining_capacity.reason).

basis.description: CLOSED enum of estimate bases. For now the single value tax_lot_only: the estimate rests on the selected tax lot(s), not a verified zoning lot (D-090-R108). New bases are appended additively only by an accepted contract task.

label.description: The scope label shown on the headline cards and exported drawings, byte-exact as the owner wrote it (D-090-R108).

assumptions.description: The assumed conditions behind this estimate, each disclosed in plain English (D-090-R108). May be empty. The face shows each entry's statement.

scope_lot.description: The tax lot this estimate is for (D-090-R108). Every field is derived deterministically from the BBL by the emitter; the face shows display.

bbl.description: The 10-digit BBL the lot fields are derived from, e.g. '4073340070'.

borough.description: The borough display name, one of the five, derived from the BBL's borough digit.

block.description: Tax block as digits with no leading zeros, e.g. '7334' (derived from the BBL's 5-digit block with leading zeros stripped).

lot.description: Tax lot as digits with no leading zeros, e.g. '70' (derived from the BBL's 4-digit lot with leading zeros stripped).

display.description: The human lot label shown on the face, e.g. 'Queens block 7334, lot 70'.

scope_whole_site.description: Whole-site development stays UNCONFIRMED (D-090-R108): the estimate is based on the selected lots, not a verified zoning lot.

status.description: Whole-site development is not confirmed by this tax-lot-only estimate.

statement.const: Based on the lots you selected — the app does not verify the zoning lot
statement.description: The existing lot-selection statement, byte-exact (equals results.lot_selection_statement and the engine constant LOT_SELECTION_STATEMENT), including the em dash (U+2014).

scope_remaining_capacity.description: Remaining development capacity stays NOT CONFIRMED (owner-settled wording, D-090-R038 / R108). Never a number. The face shows label then reason.

status.description: Remaining development capacity is not confirmed.

label.description: The owner-settled label (D-090-R038 verbatim, owner 2026-10-01; cited again by D-090-R108), byte-exact with NO final period: it equals the engine display constant UNUSED_FLOOR_AREA_NOT_AVAILABLE_TEXT (services/api/app/scenario/constants.py) byte-for-byte. The separate reason line below carries its own final period.

reason.const: Needs verified zoning-lot boundaries and existing zoning floor area.
reason.description: The owner-settled reason, byte-exact (equals the engine constant REMAINING_NOT_CONFIRMED_REASON in the three_answers package and UNUSED_FLOOR_AREA_NOT_AVAILABLE_REASON_TEXT in scenario/constants.py; both carry the final period), including the final period.

scope_assumption.description: One disclosed assumption behind the estimate (D-090-R108), e.g. the assumed corner conditions. The face shows statement.

key.description: Stable machine key, e.g. lot_type, within_100_ft_of_street_line_intersection, street_line_intersection_angle_degrees, housing_program, floor_to_floor_ft.

unit.description: The unit of value in plain words, or null when the value is dimensionless (a type, a flag, an angle in degrees carried in the key).

basis.description: Where the value came from: assumed (a stated assumption the app made), entered (the architect typed it), fixture (a fixed benchmark value), city_records (recorded city data), survey_entered (from a survey the architect supplied), approximate_tax_map (the approximate city tax map), or default (the app's default when nothing was supplied).

statement.description: A plain-English sentence stating the assumption and why, e.g. 'Corner lot assumed; the live data does not record the lot type'. Shown on the face.

street_width_case.description: One case of the plan section 4 side-by-side display for unknown street widths.

assumptions.description: The width assumed in this case for each street whose width is unknown.

assumed.description: Wide-street or narrow-street case (ZR 12-10 definitions; the width itself stays unknown).

street_width_fact_id.description: The site fact (key street_width, rank unknown) this case stands in for.

side_by_side_with.description: results_id of the other case document(s) for the same study, option and revision, shown beside this one.

unit.description: Unit vocabulary shared by results, report_model and benchmark_lot.

zr_section.description: A Zoning Resolution citation such as 'ZR 23-22', 'ZR 23-432', 'ZR 23-344(a)' or 'ZR Appendix F' (plan section 9a item 5 traceability). Whether the section exists in the CURRENT Resolution is checked by the validation suite (check C-7), not by this pattern.

value_source.description: What a number was computed from: a site fact (by fact_id), a rule table (rule_id@version), or a Zoning Resolution section.

exception_label.description: At most ONE exception beside a number, only one that changes how to read it (plan section 5a item 3 examples; plan section 8 short flags for a split district and unpermitted work on record); null otherwise. CLOSED enum; new flags are appended additively.

not_available.description: 'Not available' with the reason, in place of a number (plan section 5, section 8), e.g. 'Envelope not available — height rules for this district are not built yet'.

reason_kind.description: Which section 5 condition failed: a missing number, a missing or unreviewed rule, unresolved eligibility, or unsupported geometry (plan sections 5 and 8).

measurement.description: The measurement label of this answer's weakest input (plan section 4 'How labels carry through'). In a street_width_case document the assumed width counts as an 'assumed' input.

building_option_answer.description: The building-option answer (plan section 5 answer 3). Same oneOf as 'answer' - available or not_available - but the available branch adds the OPTIONAL additive 'notes' array (contract 1.2.0, D-090-R132). Only the building option uses this shape; floor_area_allowance and permitted_envelope use the plain 'answer' shape with no notes slot. The not-available branch is the shared answer_not_available shape, so a withheld building option may carry the 1.3.0 resolved_by / gap_kind fields.

building_option_answer_available.description: An available building-option answer: the answer_available shape (status, values, measurement) PLUS the OPTIONAL additive 'notes' array (contract 1.2.0, D-090-R132). Every valid 1.0.0 / 1.1.0 building option (no notes key) stays valid byte-for-byte because notes is optional and absent is allowed.

measurement.description: The measurement label of this answer's weakest input (plan section 4 'How labels carry through'). In a street_width_case document the assumed width counts as an 'assumed' input.

notes.description: OPTIONAL additive notes on the building option (contract 1.2.0, D-090-R132). Each entry is a COMPUTED, plain-English DRAFT reading of the captured Zoning Resolution text (e.g. the minimum-base-height note the engine computes when the built height is below the minimum base height; DB-119), carried into the results document so a surface can show it beside the heights. Absent, null or empty are all valid and leave the contract version unconstrained; a NON-EMPTY array binds contract_version to 1.2.0 (the version-binding allOf above). A note is NEVER a legal determination: each entry's 'draft' is const true and 'register' is the fixed draft-register string, documenting that the text is a draft reading pending qualified review (no 'complies' wording).

building_option_note.description: One COMPUTED, plain-English note on the building option (contract 1.2.0, D-090-R132), computed from the numbers it names (the C-11 no-template-sentences discipline). It is a DRAFT reading of the captured Zoning Resolution text, NEVER a legal determination: 'draft' is const true and 'register' is the fixed draft-register string - the not-free guard that keeps the text a draft reading pending qualified review (CLAUDE.md principle 1; D-090-R010/R118). The text must not assert compliance (no 'complies' / 'non-compliant' / 'misstate' formulation); which captured provision governs and its legal effect wait for qualified review (G6).

text.description: The note as shown: a plain-English draft reading computed from the named values, naming the Zoning Resolution sections and the pinned snapshots it rests on. Never a compliance determination.

kind.description: CLOSED enum of note kinds. For now the single value minimum_base_height: the built height is below the minimum base height and no captured provision requires the building to rise to it (D-090-R107). New kinds are appended additively only by an accepted contract task.

computed_from.description: The value keys (answer value keys or named figures) the note was computed from, e.g. ['building_height', 'min_base_height', 'max_base_height'].

values.description: The numbers (or short strings) the note was computed from, keyed by the names in computed_from, e.g. {"building_height": 20, "min_base_height": 30, "max_base_height": 45}. Each value is a number or a string; the face reads these, never a typed figure.

zr_sections.description: The Zoning Resolution sections the draft reading cites, e.g. ['ZR 23-431', 'ZR 23-432', 'ZR 23-433'].

snapshot_ids.description: The pinned ZR snapshot ids backing the draft reading, e.g. ['zr-23-431', 'zr-23-432', 'zr-23-433'].

draft.description: Const true: the not-free guard (D-090-R132). A building-option note is ALWAYS a draft reading of the captured text pending qualified review, never a reviewed or compliance statement; false is not admitted.

register.const: draft reading of the captured text
register.description: The fixed draft-register string, byte-exact. Together with draft const true it marks the note as a draft reading pending qualified review (D-090-R118), never a legal determination.

answer_value.description: One number of an answer with its unit, Zoning Resolution sections and sources (plan section 9a item 5: every number shows its section).

key.description: Stable machine key, e.g. max_residential_floor_area, max_building_height, achieved_zoning_floor_area. The same keys are used by benchmark_lot expected values.

value_sf.description: Zoning floor area that can still be added; 0 when the existing building already uses or exceeds the allowance (see existing_building.larger_than_allowed_flag).

existing_zoning_floor_area_fact_id.description: The site fact (key existing_zoning_floor_area) that was subtracted. Recorded building area is never subtracted (plan section 3 step 4, section 8).

sq_ft.description: Allowance minus the building option's achieved zoning floor area.

shortfall_reason.description: One reason, computed from real constraints and true (check C-11: no template sentences such as 'another floor would exceed the height limit' unless computed as true). It names the constraints it was computed from and the numbers compared.

computed_from.description: Constraint ids (answer value keys or rule ids) the reason was computed from.

values.description: The numbers compared, e.g. {name: 'height_with_one_more_floor', value: 62, unit: 'feet'} and {name: 'max_building_height', value: 55, unit: 'feet'}.

group.description: Add-on catalog group (plan section 6): A as-of-right, B certification, C neighbor, D1 approval with a text maximum. D2 never produces a number.

relative_to.description: Gains are always relative to the current selection (plan section 5; M1-25).

requires.description: What the add-on requires, in plain English.

floor_area_sf.description: Change in zoning floor area; may be negative for a trade-off such as ground-floor commercial space (plan section 6).

excluded.description: Every add-on left out, with why (plan section 5). Group C and D1 add-ons are never part of Best combination.

goal_value_sf.description: The goal's floor area achieved by the combination (e.g. residential zoning floor area for the default goal).

floor_use.description: Use of a floor or plate; the same kinds the drawing style table colors (plan section 5c item 5).

floor_row.description: One row of the floor-by-floor table. zoning_floor_area_sf = gross_sf - deductions_sf (checked by the consistency sweep, check C-5). Phase 1 has no building-code deductions (plan section 2).

floor.description: 1 = ground floor; 0 and below = cellar levels. The same numbering is used by floor_stack and geometry.floor_plates.

floor_label.description: Display name read by every drawing and table (check C-4: floor names come from results).

floors_fit.description: How many floors fit under the height limits with the option's floor-to-floor heights.

allowable_area_sf.description: Allowable area of this floor inside the envelope, including where setbacks shrink upper floors.

paths.description: The three paths side by side, each with its floor area, height and rule (plan section 5b table).

partial_rebuild.description: Path 2: an available result always carries its rebuild budget (plan section 5b; task M2-08).

partial_rebuild_traps.description: Traps flagged on path 2 (plan section 5b 'Traps the app flags on path 2'); empty when none applies.

items.description: walls_new_development = removing more than 75% of the floor area and more than 25% of the perimeter walls, then replacing them, counts as a new development; unsafe_condition_75_percent = if a Buildings Department order for an unsafe condition brings total removal to 75%, the protection is lost.

exceptions.description: Exceptions shown only when they apply (plan section 5b).

flags.description: Section 5b flags: rent-regulated apartments (demolition needs state approval and tenant relocation), recorded zoning-lot documents, and a large gap between recorded building area and zoning floor area.

headline.description: When path 1 or 2 keeps more floor area than path 3, the plain statement 'Keeping the building preserves N sq ft that a new building could not have.' (plan section 5b; task M2-08); null otherwise.

anyOf.pattern: ^Keeping the building preserves [0-9]{1,3}(,[0-9]{3})* sq ft that a new building could not have\.$

larger_than_allowed_flag.description: The one flag shown when the existing building is larger than today's allowance (plan section 8 wording; check C-3); null otherwise.

anyOf.const: The existing building is larger than today's zoning allows; demolition would reduce floor area.

rule.description: The rule behind the path in plain English (plan section 5b).

rebuild_budget.description: Path 2 only: the floor area and outer-wall length that may be removed (plan section 5b); null for paths 1 and 3.

rounding_rule.description: The rounding rule in words, e.g. 'rounds up only at .75 or more'.

point.description: [x, y] in feet in the geometry block's CRS.

ring.description: Closed ring (first and last points equal), at least four points.

polygon.description: Exterior ring first, then any holes.

yard_not_required.description: A yard the rules do not require here, stated so no drawing shows it (competitor review: a 20 ft rear yard drawn where none is required).

geometry_available.description: Available geometry. The lot outline (with its crs, units, measurement label and streets) is always present; each rule-dependent layer - yards, setback lines, envelope, floor plates - is independently available or not_available with its reason (G3 RC-1), so the site plan and the DXF lot layer exist even where height rules are not built yet (plan section 3 step 7 separate DXF layers; section 5 'Every supported answer still shows'; tasks M1-15, M1-16; section 11 Pilot B).

crs.description: local_feet = a local plane in feet with its origin at a lot corner and its axes parallel to the EPSG:2263 grid (+x = grid east, +y = grid north; the site plan's north arrow is grid north); EPSG:2263 = NY State Plane Long Island (US survey feet). Never EPSG:4326 display coordinates (plan section 4 'Coordinates'). Coordinates are never shown to or edited by the architect.

measurement.description: Measurement label of the lot outline; drives the DXF and drawing note, e.g. 'Approximate — city tax map, not a survey' (plan section 3 step 7).

streets.description: Each street the lot fronts: its name, its frontage line on the lot outline, and the street_width site fact that labels its width on the site plan (plan section 5c item 2; check C-4: labels are read from results). Empty only when no frontage is known.

street_width_fact_id.description: fact_id of the street_width site fact; null when the study has none for this street.

yards.description: Yards layer, or not_available when the yard rules are not built.

setback_lines_per_level.description: Setback lines for each floor where a setback applies, in plan (plan section 5 'Floor stack'); not_available when the height and setback rules are not built.

envelope.description: The permitted envelope as stacked tiers (each an outline extruded from bottom_ft to top_ft), or not_available with its reason - e.g. height rules not built - while the lot outline still shows.

floor_plates.description: The building option's floor plate per floor (plan section 5c item 1); gross_sf equals the floor_by_floor row of the same floor (check C-4). not_available when the building option is not available.

status.description: Rule lifecycle status, the same vocabulary as rule_evaluation.schema.json rule_status. 'published' requires qualified-reviewer approval (CLAUDE.md principle 12; D-090-R010).
